Commentary.Commentary: Right then! Pakistan will have to bat out of their skins if they are to get anywhere closer to the New Zealand total. Will they be able to get a solid start to their batting innings? Answers coming up shortly on the other side of this short break.

On the bowling by the visitors, they started on a good note as Shaheen Afridi snared a couple of quick wickets but soon the fizz cooled down as they started leaking runs. Afridi though ended with a 4-wicket haul, Yasir Shah had three to his name too. Whereas, Naseem, Abbas and Ashraf had a wicket each to their name. All the frontline bowlers of Pakistan ended up being on the expensive side as they failed to get wickets regularly and that meant that they are staring at a huge first innings lead.

Though Taylor departed after a well made 70 runs, Williamson continued in the company of Henry Nicholls and stitched another stand in excess of 100 runs as he brought up his 23rd Test ton too. Nicholls too was good as he got to his half ton too. But a poor decision to not review a caught behind cost him his wicket. Williamson too followed soon as Watling got to another half ton and stitched 66-run stand with Kyle Jamieson. Some lower order contributions meant that New Zealand ended with a healthy total on board.

A brilliant innings from New Zealand after being put into bat by the visitors. The way they started getting this far looked a far fetch dream but the Blackcaps have done it. Thanks to some brilliant batting contributions. Having lost two quick wickets, New Zealand wanted a partnership to bring them back on track and they got one in the form of Williamson-Taylor stand as the duo added 120 runs.

Pakistan during the entire first hour looked clueless, hapless and out of ideas as they were easily taken for runs. After facing the heat for the entire 60 minutes the refreshment break brought some relief to them as soon after the break they succeeded in breaking the 133-run stand between Williamson and Nicholls to get a foot back into the game. As is the norm one brings two and that continued as a brilliant piece of fielding by Haris Sohail off the bowling of Yasir Shah. Meanwhile, Kane Williamson went past his 23rd Test ton as Nicholls got to a fifty of his own. Though Nicholls innings was cut short after he edged out behind which later the replays showed to be gone off the forearm and not the glove but Nicholls had departed by then. Though Kane Williamson continued to grind the Pakistan bowlers and get on the run making spree. Just when it felt like there is no one who could get Williamson out, the reality struck and Williamson departed after a well made 129 runs. New Zealand are well placed at the moment with the pair of Watling and Santner out there in the middle.

We are all set to begin Day 2 as the two overnight batsmen Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls will resume their innings for New Zealand. Pakistan players are out in the middle too and are ready to go as well. Mohammad Abbas will start the proceedings for Day 2. Here we go...
Who will come out on top? How long will New Zealand bat? Many of such questions would be answered as the day unfolds. Stay tuned for the same as we bring you all the coverage of the game.

Coming to Pakistan now, they started brilliantly but a few dropped chances and a missed review opportunity against Kane Williamson has made their task a lot difficult. Though the new ball is just 7 overs old and if Pakistan can make some early inroads in the morning session then it could be another enthralling day.

After an absorbing day of Day 1 of a Test match we move onto Day 2. Hello and welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of the first Test between New Zealand and Pakistan. Having recovered from 13/2, New Zealand finished the day with three down and 222 runs on the board. The good news for them is their ever reliable skipper is still unbeaten on 94 runs and they would hope that he goes on to score a daddy hundred and take New Zealand to a total from where they can win easily.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Right then! That ends the engrossing Day 1 of the Boxing Day Test. New Zealand with their noses slightly ahead at the moment would look to come out blazing on Day 2 and look to pile on the misery on the Pakistan bowlers. Whereas, Pakistan would look to capitalise on the morning session and the new ball. Let's see who stamps their authority on Day 2? Do join us for that at 1100 local (2200 GMT). Till then, cheers and take care.

Ross Taylor is down for a quick chat. Let's hear it from him. He says that when he started his career, he was happy to play just one or two games but having come this long and far makes him feel happy. He further mentions that he did not hear the announcement but he was congratulated by a few Pakistani players when he walked out to bat. On the pitch, he says that entire summer the surfaces have been green but this one here is not that green as the last two games. He further says that they are happy with where they are placed at the end of the day. Mentions that they did not start well as they lost a couple of quick wickets. Praises Shaheen Afridi as he mentions that he did not give away any scoring opportunity. Ends by saying that the margin of error on these New Zealand tracks is minimal and he hopes that the surface starts to show its tricks cometh Day 4 and Day 5.

Coming to the hosts now, they did not begin well as they lost a couple of quick wickets. Once again, the Kiwi team and the dressing room laid their hopes and eyes on the experienced duo of Kane Williamson and Ross Taylor. The pair slowly and steadily started building on the platform and in the process, both went past their respective fifties as they stitched a 120-run stand for the 3rd wicket. Though Taylor departed after a well compiled 70 runs, Williamson continued his good work as he remained unbeaten on 94 runs and with him is Henry Nicholls who also is unbeaten on 42 runs. The duo have added 89 runs so far.

After a wicketless second session for the visitors, they came back in the third to send a well set Ross Taylor for 70-odd runs. They did bowl well as they kept it simple and tight with a lot of discipline but they failed to pick wickets regularly. To add to it, a couple of dropped catches off Kane Williamson and a missed LBW review haunted them as the Kiwi skipper made them pay heavily.

Starting with the visitors first up, after electing to field first, Pakistan began on the right note as on the third ball of the match Shaheen Afridi sent Tom Latham back into the hut. He along with Mohammad Abbas, made life difficult for the Kiwi batsmen as Afridi snared the second one in the form of Tom Blundell. Having put New Zealand in a spot of bother with the score 13/2, Pakistan seemed to have lost its steam as they failed to pick wickets or contain the run flow.

A day which began on a good note for the visitors ends on a better note for the hosts. Brilliant Day 1 of a Test match where there was even contest between bat and ball. Also, what Craig MacMillan had told earlier during the pitch report came true. The bowlers got all the assistance from the surface and the batters once they got their eyes in then the run-scoring became easier.

Length ball around off, Kane blocks it out with an open stance.
Length and down the leg side, Kane lets it be.
Ohhs and Ahhs from Pakistan players! Length ball around off, Blundell once again makes a confident leave. A maiden from Abbas.

A huge shout from Abbas but the umpire is unmoved. Length ball around off, Blundell looks to defend it off the front foot but gets a huge inside edge onto his pads. The bowler though appeals but nothing from the umpire.
Short of a good length around off, Tom keeps it out off the back foot this time.
Good length and around off, Blundell defends it off the back foot towards short leg.
Length ball around off, this time a bit closer to the sticks as Blundell blocks it off the front foot.
Abbas starts with a length ball around off, Blundell is aware of his off pole as he makes a confident leave.
Mohammad Abbas to bowl from the other end.

End of a brilliant first over from Afridi. He almost gets a second one. Length and slanting across the right-hander. Williamson has a feel for it as he pokes his bat out. Lucky for him the ball sneaks past the outside edge.
On a length and around off, Williamson turns it to short leg this time.

A huge shout there from Afridi but nothing from the umpire. Fuller and around middle and leg, Williamson looks to tuck it to the leg side but gets beaten and out comes the appeal but the umpire is unmoved.
Kane Williamson is the new batsman in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Afridi strikes and Latham has to depart! Length and around off, Latham is still not sure whether to play off the front foot or the back foot as he hangs his bat out. The ball takes the outside edge and flies towards the third slip fielder. Azhar Ali there takes it on the second attempt and New Zealand have been dealt a blow early on in the innings.
Length and  outside off, left alone by Latham this time.

EDGED AND FOUR! Afridi is right on the money! Bowls a length ball around off, Latham is in two minds as to how to play the ball. He decides to play it off the back foot and manages to get a thick outside edge and the ball flies past the gully fielder and into the fence behind. New Zealand off the mark.

Done and dusted with the National Anthems as we are all set to begin the first day of the Boxing Day Test. The two New Zealand openers, Tom Blundell and Tom Latham are out to start the New Zealand innings. Pakistan players too are on the field after a few final words from their new skipper, Mohammad Rizwan. Shaheen Afridi will start the proceedings for Pakistan.
Players from both the teams now come out and line up for their respective National Anthems. It will be Pakistan's first followed by New Zealand's.

Pitch Report - Craig MacMillan says that the weather is brilliant as the sun is out there in its full glory. Grant Elliot joins him and says that it is still a lesser grassed surface unlike the previous two Tests against West Indies. He also mentions that there will be pace and bounce and if the bowlers pitch it up then there is a chance of getting some swing. He further mentions that if the pitch dries up then the spinners can have a say on Day 4 and Day 5. MacMillan ends by saying that though the surface has something in for the pacers but if the batters hold their fort then there are runs on offer too.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham, Tom Blundell, Kane Williamson (C), Ross Taylor, Henry Nicholls, BJ Watling (WK), Mitchell Santner, Kyle Jamieson, Tim Southee, Neil Wagner, Trent Boult.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Shan Masood, Abid Ali, Azhar Ali, Fawad Alam, Haris Sohail, Mohammad Rizwan (WK/C), Faheem Ashraf, Yasir Shah, Mohammad Abbas, Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah.

New Zealand skipper, Kane Williamson says that it is a good day and they too were looking to bowl. Mentions that it is a different location and how the surface will react they will see. Mentions that Pakistan have been here before and they are a quality side. Also, praises Ross Taylor for his batting skills and his contribution towards New Zealand cricket after he became the most capped player for New Zealand.

Pakistan skipper, Mohammad Rizwan says that they will bowl first. He says that with the green tinge on the pitch they want to take the early advantage. Also mentions that the guys are confident to perform here against New Zealand. He also mentions that the conditions are a bit difficult in New Zealand and they also got just 3 days of practice but they are raring to go out and perform.

TOSS - It's time for the flip of the coin. The two skippers are out in the middle along with the match referee. Kane has the coin as he gives it a toss. Rizwan calls heads. It lands in favour of Rizwan. PAKISTAN ELECT TO FIELD!

Whereas, with the bat Latham, Williamson and Taylor are on fire and New Zealand having batted just twice in the last two Tests would look to do the same.
